text: This is a common side effect of vaccines and is your immune system's natural response to the vaccine. This is expected and usually starts a few hours after getting the injection and settles within a few days. Some vaccines, such as the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine, can cause a delayed reaction. This could be a high fever (over 39 C) between 6 and 12 days after immunisation and temporary joint pain 2 to 4 weeks after immunisation. To ease the fever you can dress lightly, with a single layer of clothing, keep the room cool, use a fan and drink plenty of fluids. Because paracetamol or ibuprofen can interfere with your immune response to a vaccine, only take them for relief of significant discomfort or high fever.
